name: Upper Blue Lake Dam Campground
note: PG&E-operated campground at the dam on Upper Blue Lake, a PG&E project reservoir in the Blue Lakes basin ~11 mi up gravel Blue Lakes Rd off Hwy 88 at Carson Pass; ~25 drive-in sites, first-come, first-served. --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservations need at least 2 nights (max 14) and can't be made within 3 days of arrival; reservations for the season open April 15. Some sites are first-come, first-served, and those can be taken for a single night. Kept per AWH 2026-10-10: the FCFS sites mean a one-night stay is possible.
field_notes.Fees: PG&E reservation site, July 6-8 2027 search (2-night 'Use Fee' halved; 3-night check at Lake McCumber confirmed it is the stay total). $27/night at Upper Blue Lake Dam Site, $25 at the Dam Site Expansion. Other fees and taxes may apply; cancellation $15 per site.

name: Eagle Creek Campground
note: Shasta-Trinity NF campground on the upper Trinity River near the Eagle Creek confluence, Hwy 3 north of Trinity Center, 17-18 sites, drinking water, vault toilets, RVs/trailers to 35 ft; open roughly mid-May to late August. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open roughly mid-May to late August.

name: Trapper Springs Campground
note: PG&E-operated campground near the west shore of Courtright Reservoir (within Sierra NF), ~8,200 ft, off McKinley Grove/Courtright Rd. 70 drive-in sites described by the Forest Service as 'relatively flat and good for large RVs' but without lake views. Reservable through PG&E recreation. --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservations need at least 2 nights (max 14) and can't be made within 3 days of arrival; reservations for the season open April 15. Some sites are first-come, first-served, and those can be taken for a single night. Kept per AWH 2026-10-10: the FCFS sites mean a one-night stay is possible.
field_notes.Fees: PG&E reservation site, July 6-8 2027 search (2-night 'Use Fee' halved; 3-night check at Lake McCumber confirmed it is the stay total). $24/night, all sites. Other fees and taxes may apply; cancellation $15 per site.

name: Sherwin Creek Campground
note: Inyo NF campground ~2 mi from Mammoth Lakes along aspen-lined Sherwin Creek (elev ~7,600 ft); 87 sites, RVs to 60 ft (most 35-40), no hookups, water, vault toilets, RV fill station, bear lockers; Sherwin Lakes trailhead adjacent. Reservable, open ~mid-May to early Sep. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open about mid-May to early September.

name: Paradise Shores RV Park
note: Family-owned RV park & campground on the shore of Bridgeport Reservoir off Hwy 182, Eastern Sierra. Full-hookup drive-in RV sites plus a few tent sites and rental trailers; restrooms/showers, laundry, dump station; typically a 2-3 night minimum in season (5 over the 4th of July), none on same-day bookings. Blue-ribbon trout fishing (reservoir + East Walker River). --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: typically 2-3 nights in season, 5 over the 4th of July; none on same-day bookings (paradiseshorescamp.com, 2026-10-12). --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights, 5 on holidays (4th of July)

field_notes.Booking: Typically 2-3 nights through the season and 5 over the 4th of July for RV and tent sites; no minimum on same-day reservations (operator's camping page).

name: Haskins Valley Campground
note: PG&E-operated campground on the south shore of Bucks Lake, 16731 Bucks Lake Rd, Quincy. 65 sites; a few sites fit RVs up to 30 ft, most best for tents. Reservable through PG&E; sites 10 and 14-29 are first-come, first-served. --Claude  Bucks Lake drawn down below normal after Labor Day 2026 for dam repairs; boat ramps unusable from about mid-September 2026 (PG&E notice, 2026-10-10). --Claude  First-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open early June to early October.
field_notes.Booking: Reservations need at least 2 nights (max 14) and can't be made within 3 days of arrival; reservations for the season open April 15. Some sites are first-come, first-served, and those can be taken for a single night. Kept per AWH 2026-10-10: the FCFS sites mean a one-night stay is possible.
field_notes.Fees: PG&E reservation site, July 6-8 2027 search (2-night 'Use Fee' halved; 3-night check at Lake McCumber confirmed it is the stay total). $30/night, all sites. Other fees and taxes may apply; cancellation $15 per site.

name: Camping du Parc de l'Île Melville
note: Municipal nonprofit outdoor park (Parc de l'Île Melville) in Shawinigan, along the Saint-Maurice River; 152 sites — 107 with 3 services, 14 water/electric, 24 unserviced — plus 6 cabins, pool, boat launch, trails. Open early May–mid-Oct, reservable. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open early May to mid-October.

name: Algonquin Pines Campground
note: Family campground on Hwy 60 at Dwight, about 20 km west of Algonquin Provincial Park's West Gate and 23 km from Huntsville. Listed at 143 drive-in sites — 43 pull-throughs, 15 full-hookup and 98 hydro/water sites on 15/30 amp — plus glamping tents and a cabin. Washroom/shower buildings, coin laundry, camp store, dump station, pool, mini-putt, playground and covered pavilion. Open Victoria Day long weekend to Thanksgiving. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Victoria Day long weekend to Thanksgiving.
field_notes.Fees: 2024: unserviced sites from C$52 a night (+ taxes and fees)

name: Brennan Harbour RV Park
note: Small owner-operated RV park on Bushwell Bay off the North Channel of Georgian Bay (Lake Huron), east of Spanish. 42 sites, all with metered 30/50-amp hydro, water and full sewer (pump-out); back-ins listed to 50 ft; shaded, sunny and water-front sites plus limited boat dockage. Site mix is mostly leased seasonal, but the operator's rate sheet explicitly lists 'transient sites available' with 30/50-amp hydro and water at $60-80 CAD daily ($360-480 weekly), so nightly RV camping is a standing product. No tents allowed; RV/trailer units older than 15 years may be refused. Open early May to mid-October (Thanksgiving). Book by phone/email reservation form; no online booking engine. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open early May to mid-October (Thanksgiving).

name: Linamac Lodge & Trailer Park
note: 40-acre partially wooded campground on Lake Louise, on Hwy 129 about 20 km (15 minutes) south of Chapleau. Over 50 full-service sites offered for overnight, weekly or seasonal use, all with drinking water, 30-50 amp electric, septic, fire pit and picnic table; drive-through sites suit motorhomes and trailers, plus tent areas and housekeeping cabins. Renovated shower house, game room, camp shop, playground, private sandy beach with paddle boats, kayaks, SUPs and a floating trampoline; ATV and logging-road trails from the property. Open mid-May to mid-October, weather permitting; reserve by phone or email. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open mid-May to mid-October, weather permitting.

name: McGowan Lake Campground
note: 226 gravel-pad sites on McGowan Lake at 21321 Highway 7, Maberly, in Lanark County; mix of seasonal and overnight camping. Unserviced, premium unserviced (water only), 15-amp serviced, 30-amp serviced; maximum of four adults. Sandy beach, store, laundry, showers, dump station, two playgrounds, dog park, rec hall. Open May 1 to Oct 1; credit card holds a reservation, 48-hour cancellation. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: McGowan Lake: serviced sites, water and 15-amp C$50 a day, 30-amp C$60; unserviced C$35; plus HST. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Red Bay Tent & Trailer Park
note: Family-run park in the hamlet of Red Bay on the Bruce Peninsula, 428 Huron Rd. 75 sites total — 55 seasonal plus a transient block of 8 overnight serviced RV sites, 5 overnight tent sites and 5 unserviced wilderness sites. Serviced sites are 30 amp hydro, sewer and potable water; max RV length 34 ft. 2026 overnight rates $55/night wilderness (3-night minimum on long weekends, $10 reservation fee). Open early May to Thanksgiving (approx May 7 - Oct 11). Reserve by email/phone with a one-night non-refundable deposit. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Red Bay: serviced (30-amp, sewer, water) C$69 a night, C$75 on long weekends with a 3-night minimum; plus 13% HST; C$10 reservation fee. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Smith's Trailer Park & Camp
note: Long-running family park (in operation over 90 years) on the east shore of Little Lake in Midland, minutes from town. 147 sites split between a fully-booked seasonal section and an overnight section; the operator's site map shows numbered loops on Stan's Circle, Minnow/Catfish/Perch/Bass Drives and Lakeshore Road with 30-amp and 50-amp electric, water and sewer, paved roads and gravel pads, plus pull-thrus.  No tent camping.  Beach on Little Lake, pool, store, propane, laundry, playground.  Overnight season runs mid-May to October; reservations through CampLife.  A separate mobile-home park adjoins the campground at the office end. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Overnight season mid-May to October.
field_notes.Fees: Read on CampLife (2026-10-14): one night on an overnight site in June 2027 is C$54.23 before HST, and each stay also carries a flat C$9. The park's own site posts no rate.

name: Point Wolfe Campground
note: Fundy NP coastal campground ~8 km west of the east entrance, reached across the Point Wolfe covered bridge — max vehicle/equipment length 7.3 m (24 ft) and height 4.4 m (13 ft), so a 23-ft rig fits. 155 drive-in sites: 24 electric/water, 120 unserviced (+10 oTENTiks, 1 Ôasis). Washrooms/showers, dump station; cell reception extremely limited. Reservable, open ~late June to early Sept. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Open about late June to early September.

name: Hyclass Ocean Campground
note: Campground at Havre Boucher with ocean-view RV sites and, in the E section, primitive sites out on the point.  Swimming is off the dock, in what the campground calls the warmest waters north of the Carolinas; there is no sandy beach, so water shoes are recommended, and there are canoes, kayaks and pedal boats.  There is beach-side volleyball, washer toss, a playground, a small walking trail, birdwatching (more than 30 kinds seen) and a book exchange.  Two cabins and a fifth-wheel trailer are rented, there are seasonal sites, and cyclists get a special rate for one tent.  Quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Read on Campspot: one night for 2 adults, site rate before tax, every RV site type a 23-ft rig fits (Primitive - Ocean Front Tent/RV sites, Power and Water 30 Amp Back in RV Site, Pull-Through Electric and Water Site - Not completely level, Full Hook Up 30amp Back in RV Site and Pull-Through Ocean View RV Site - Full Hook Up). June 2027: C$39-50, Tuesday and Saturday alike. Campspot shows the park closed in October 2026. Campspot offers no sites in January 2027. Left out: Primitive - Ocean View - Tent/RV, Primitive Tent/RV Site, Tent/RV Site 15 Amp Electric and Water (sites under 23 ft). Plus the park's C$6 'Booking Fee', once per stay. Read 2026-10-13. The campground's rate page, before 14% HST, lists the same C$45 a night for an RV or van site with water and 15- or 30-amp power, C$50 for a 3-way ocean-view site (30 amps) and C$39 for a small RV or tent on a waterfront E-section site with no services.

name: Lockeport Campground & Cottages
note: Private campground near Lockeport (Lydgate, off Hwy 3). Mix of unserviced tent sites, a 20-amp powered tent site, serviced 30-amp RV sites (2-way power/water with dump access; 3-way power/water/sewer), plus bunkies and cottages; also seasonal sites (Apr 25–Oct 25). Heated saltwater pool; nightly transient RV camping available. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: 2026: 30A power and water C$48, 30A three-way service C$52, plus HST; max 2 adults and 3 children.

name: Wild Nature Campground
note: Family-owned campground near Shubenacadie, about 45 minutes from Halifax, beside Lynch Lake (swimming at your own risk), with trails, free Wi-Fi and hot showers.  The 30-amp full-service sites are for RVs only, pull-through or back-in, to 70 ft; the 15-amp and unserviced lake-view sites take tents or RVs to 40 ft, back-in only, and the wooded unserviced sites RVs to 20 ft, and there is a group site. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Read on Campspot: one night for 2 adults, site rate before tax, every RV site type a 23-ft rig fits (Electricity ONLY 15 AMP Lake View Site, Lake View Un-Serviced Site, 30 AMP Back-In RV Site and 30 AMP Pull-Through RV Site). October 2026 and June 2027: C$35-45 on a Tuesday; C$40-50 on a Saturday. Campspot shows the park closed in January 2027. Left out: Wooded Un-Serviced Site (sites under 23 ft). Plus the park's C$5 'Reservation Fee', once per stay. Read 2026-10-13.

name: Yogi Bear's Jellystone Park Camp Resort
note: Family camp-resort in the Annapolis Valley at Kingston (43 Boo Boo Blvd); graduated RV sites from 15-amp field sites to 30/50-amp full-hookup deluxe and VIP angled drive-thru pads (fitting long rigs), plus tent sites and rental cabins; 2-night minimum. Reservable online. --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on every stay, 3 on long weekends; one night only by emailed request (jellystonens.com policy, 2026-10-12). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservations need 2 nights, 3 on long weekends; a one-night stay can be requested by email at least 7 days ahead, subject to approval (operator's policy).
field_notes.Fees: Season-dependent: low-season weekday C$39, weekend C$49; high-season weekday C$55, weekend C$65; themed weekends C$69.

name: Banting Memorial Municipal Park
note: Town of Musgrave Harbour municipal park ~8 km south of town on Rte 330 (Kittiwake Coast), on a saltwater pond beside an ocean beach. 50/30-amp power+water and water-only drive-in sites; comfort station with washrooms, showers and laundromat; dump station; interpretation centre, playground, walking trail. Seasonal sites available; open ~mid-Jun to early Sep. Named for Sir Frederick Banting. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Let's Camp booking engine (2027): water-only C$30, 30-amp + water C$35, 50-amp + water C$40 a night, tax included. Read 2026-11-07.

name: Gooney Creek Campground
note: Family-run for 30+ years, 5 miles south of Front Royal across from the Shenandoah River. RV sites with 20/30-amp water/electric (some creekside, some full hookup), plus tent sites, a group tent site and a tiny house, most along Gooney Creek; showers, flush toilets, dump station, swimming hole. Open April 1 through November 15 (2026). Multiple reviews note noise all night long from the nearby highway bridge. One review also claims no potable water for filling an RV tank if staying at primitive sites. Book on the operator's own booking page (gooneycreekcampground.com, 'Check Availability') or by phone. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Booked online through the operator's NewBook page ('Check Availability'); self check-in instructions sent before arrival, so late arrivals are fine. Group tent site needs 10 people.
field_notes.Fees: Operator's booking page, quoted for Tue 2026-10-27 and Sat 2026-10-31 (same price both nights): electric/water 20/30-amp $48.50/night, creekside electric/water $53.50, 20/30-amp full hookup $63.50; tent $38.50, group tent $123.50, tiny house $103.50.

name: Riverside Campground
note: Family-owned campground on the North Fork Holston River about 5 miles from Abingdon and the Virginia Creeper Trail. Operator's site lists 94 full-hookup sites (30/50 amp, pull-thrus available) taken for overnight, monthly and permanent stays, plus 22-38 20-amp electric/water sites for tents and pop-ups; posted single-night rates are $35 tent (6 nights get the 7th free). Season runs April 1 to October 31; a seasonal site is $1,650/year plus metered electric, so the park mixes seasonals with a real nightly inventory. Pool, bathhouse, laundry, camp store, propane. Reservations by phone; specific sites are not guaranteed. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: 'Call to make your reservation' (276) 623-0340. A specific site is not guaranteed. Holiday rentals require a 3-night non-refundable deposit and 7 days' cancellation notice; other stays a 1-night deposit and 3 days' notice. River sites: 6 people, 2 tents, 2 vehicles, no visitors. Check-in 2 pm, check-out 11 am.
field_notes.Fees: 'Riverside Camping Rate 2025', single night: full hookup (30 or 50 amp) $43.85 + $6.15 tax = $50.00; pop-up $35.08 ($40 with tax) and tent $30.69 ($35 with tax) on the 20-amp electric/water tent and pop-up sites. Stay 6 nights, 7th free. Monthly $560 (30 amp) / $590 (50 amp) plus tax and metered electric; seasonal $1,650 a year plus electric.
field_notes.Sites: 94 full-hookup sites (30/50 amp) for overnight and monthly stays plus 22 tent and pop-up sites (20-amp electric and water, most on the river). Seasonal sites are sold too.

name: River Run Campground
note: Primitive drive-in campground on the South Fork Shenandoah River. No hookups: picnic table and fire ring per site, portable toilets serviced weekly, generators permitted, self-contained campers and RVs explicitly allowed; grass sites reached by a gravel drive along the riverbank. 17 sites the operator calls riverfront plus others with river access, and a large area for groups of 25+. 50% deposit at booking. Drive-ups accepted April 1 to October 1 and sites reservable by phone year round. Quiet time from midnight to 8 AM which is late by campground standards, so music can run well into the night. --Claude

field_notes.Season: 'River Run Campground is open year round'; drive-ups are accepted only April 1 to October 1, and outside that window sites are by reservation.
field_notes.Booking: Reserve by phone (540-683-9673) with a 50% deposit; balance on arrival by cash or card (no checks). Drive-ups accepted April 1 to October 1 only. Refund less $10 with 7+ days' notice, deposit forfeited inside 7 days. Checkout noon Monday-Saturday, 4 p.m. Sunday.
field_notes.Fees: River Run: $40 flat site fee per stay plus $40 a night per vehicle, so one night with one vehicle is $80 (the flat fee spreads over longer stays: 2 nights $120); $2 credit-card fee; 50% deposit. Read 2026-11-07.

name: Clinch River Family Campground
note: Family-owned campground on the Clinch River about 7 miles off the main highway near Duffield. Operator lists 27 full-hookup sites, 20 premium full-hookup sites on the river and 11 electric/water sites, plus 11 rustic tent sites on the riverbank; level gravel pads, 30 amp standard with limited 50 amp, big-rig friendly, boat launch, renovated bathhouse, fire pit and picnic table per site, Wi-Fi. Open year round. Rustic tent $25, E/W tent $35; weekly, monthly and long-term sites also offered. Reservable online, or by phone/text. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Online through the operator's Firefly Reservations page, or call/text 1-877-254-6247 or email. Full refund (less processing fees) on cancellation two weeks out. Check-in after 2 pm, check-out noon.
field_notes.Fees: Full hookup $40 a day with 30 amp, $45 with 50 amp (limited), for two adults; $5 per extra adult. Read 2026-10-14.
field_notes.Sites: '27 full hookup sites and 11 electric and water', '20 premium full hookup sites on the river and 11 Rustic tents sites on the riverbank'; 'Big rig friendly'. The rates page prices the electric/water sites as 'E / W Tent Sites', so the RV count may be 47.

name: Hemlock Campground of Potter County
note: Family-run (Runkle family) campground at 2084 Wharton Rd (Route 872) in Wharton Twp, southern Potter County, strung along the First Fork of Sinnemahoning Creek; RV Life counts 123 sites. The operator's campground map splits them explicitly: roughly 30 blue "Reservable RV Sites" numbered 1-33 with water and 30-amp electric, a much larger brown seasonal RV block numbered 100-196, 11 tent sites and 6 rental cabins. Published nightly rates are $30 primitive tent / $35 deluxe tent, cabins $80-120. Two catch-and-release ponds, camp store with live bait and propane, two dump stations, gem mining. Reservable online through the operator's own booking page; the operator site does not publish opening or closing dates. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Online booking through the operator's Park With Us engine: one-night minimum, same-day bookings allowed, online stays capped at 7 nights ('For reservations longer than 7 nights, please call us at (814) 647-8403').
field_notes.Fees: $50 a night for a camper site (water and 30-amp), $55 for premium site 21 (stone pad, creekside, pavilion); tent sites $30-35. Rates for 2 adults; extra adult $12, extra child $6-8 a night in the booking engine. The rates page carries no year; read live 2026-10-20 (engine site records updated 2026-09-21).
field_notes.Sites: The booking engine lists 122 RV sites and 11 tent sites (besides cabins). Only 19 RV sites are bookable online by the night (sites 9-12, 17-19, 21-23, 25-33; 12 of them pull-through, 30-45 ft); the rest (1-8, 13-16 and the 100-197 block) are not bookable and the operator map marks the 100s seasonal. Listed max lengths on bookable sites are 30-45 ft.

name: Camp Charles Campground
note: Long-established family campground at 1077 Blue Mountain Dr in Bangor (Slate Belt, ~20 min from the Delaware Water Gap NRA); RV Life counts 138 sites. The operator's 2025 site map shows roughly 130 numbered full-hookup pads on several loops around an on-site stocked lake, plus about 25 tent sites, two rental cabins and a rental RV; pool, camp store, laundry, game room, dump station and propane. Season runs April 11 to October 18, with the operator publishing a nightly water & electric campsite rate (6 nights and the 7th free) alongside seasonal ($2,350 for 2 nights/week) and all-season ($3,400 for 22 weeks) packages. The seasonal contingent is large - golf carts are restricted to seasonal campers and gate cards are issued to seasonal families - so transient sites are limited; reserve by phone or the site's inquiry form (no online booking engine). --Claude

field_notes.Season: The operator's 2025 rate sheet: 'Campground season April 11th through October 18th'.
field_notes.Booking: No online booking engine: every 'Book Now' button leads to a reservation inquiry form; otherwise call (610) 588-0553 or email.
field_notes.Fees: Water & electric campsite $65 a night in the regular season, $50 a night on discount weekends (before May and after late September), for 2 adults and 2 children; 6 nights get the 7th free ($390). Extra overnight guests $11-15 a night. Wooded and B-field sites are priced per person ($16 adult, $12 age 5-17). The rates page carries a 2025 pay-by date (seasonal 5% discount 'if paid in full by May 16th 2025'); read 2026-10-20.
